identity.title: CRISPR-Mediated PABPC1 Upregulation via ELF5 Binding Disruption Enhances Milk Protein and Lipid Biosynthesis in Goat Mammary Epithelial Cells.

content.abstract: Post-transcriptional control of milk protein and lipid production in goats remains poorly understood. Here we combined ONT full-length transcriptome sequencing with RNA pull-down coupled to LC-MS/MS to identify RNA-binding proteins associated with milk protein mRNAs, and uncovered poly(A)-binding protein cytoplasmic 1 (PABPC1) as a central regulator. PABPC1 bound the 3'UTRs of casein and lipid-related transcripts such as CSN2, CSN3, LALBA, and FASN, stabilizing these mRNAs and promoting their translation, while dose-dependently modulating alternative polyadenylation (APA) site selection to reshape 3'UTR isoform usage. ELF5 directly bound the PABPC1 promoter, repressing its transcription. CRISPR/Cas9 editing of this binding motif relieved this repression, elevating PABPC1 levels and increasing casein accumulation and triglyceride synthesis in goat mammary epithelial cells. Our findings define an ELF5-PABPC1-APA regulatory module and nominate a tractable target for molecular breeding to enhance goat milk protein and lipid content.
